title: Service allocator for plan tiers: priority scheduling with token-aging and weighted-credit heuristics
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: implement a service-allocator component that assigns incoming requests to serving lanes based on plan tier (free, paid, enterprise), real-time quota balances, and a token-aging weight so long-running customers do not starve.

Motivation: current lane allocation is largely static and leads to sharp drops for low-tier traffic during bursts and poor tail latency for customers with aged credit debt. We need a single allocator that: (1) enforces hard minimum reserves for enterprise customers, (2) opportunistically schedules paid traffic when capacity available, (3) gracefully degrades free traffic using fallback smaller model variants, and (4) smooths admission using a token-aging multiplier to prioritize customers that have been degraded frequently.

Core behaviors to implement:
- Admission scoring: compute score = base_tier_weight * normalized_quota + age_multiplier * debt_factor - latency_penalty. Higher score => higher admission priority.
- Token-aging: every time a customer's request is rejected/degraded, increment an "age" counter that increases that customer's admission multiplier until a successful admission resets it. Age increments cap at 8x multiplier.
- Quota normalization: use plan-specific bucket sizes; normalize to [0..1] by dividing remaining_quota / nominal_bucket; for enterprise use a min-reserve floor (0.15).
- Degradation policy: when admission fails for free tier, route to smaller-compatible model (quantized variant) or to cached responses if prefix hit. Paid tier should be degraded to a lower-cost variant only after enterprise reserve satisfied.
- Regional affinity: prefer local-region pools if score delta < 10% to preserve latency SLOs, otherwise route cross-region with fallback hints.
- Admission smoothing: implement leaky-bucket smoothing per-lane to avoid bursty preemption; ensure admission decisions are idempotent for retries within 2s window.

Observability and telemetry:
- New metrics: allocator.admit_rate{tier,region}, allocator.reject_reason, allocator.age_multiplier_distribution, allocator.model_fallback_rate{model_variant}.
- Dashboards: add per-plan SLO charts (p50/p95 latency, fallback rate, successful admissions) in Console -> Routing -> Allocator.

Testing & rollout plan:
1) Unit tests for scoring math and age reset behavior.
2) Integration test harness against runtime simulator with synthetic quota burn patterns (burst, slow drip, multi-tenant interference).
3) Canary rollout: 5% of traffic in us-west for 48h with detailed per-tenant histograms.
4) Gradual ramp: 5 -> 20 -> 50 -> 100 over 10 days, monitoring fallback-rate and enterprise reserve attainment.

Docs & artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RT/Allocator+Design+ENG-46290 (draft)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7682 (allocator core)
- Simulator: https://github.com/redwood-inference/tools/tree/main/allocator-sim (test vectors added)

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Should token-aging persist across deployments? (we propose in-memory with optional persisted checkpoints for very high-value tenants).
- Age multiplier cap choice: current POC uses 8x; need perf analysis to ensure free-tier can't monopolize burst windows.
- How aggressively to degrade paid -> smaller variants vs. routing to different region; leaning toward variant-first for predictable costs.

Acceptance criteria:
- Allocator passes all unit/integration tests in CI.
- Canary shows <= 2% increase in enterprise tail latency and <= 12% fallback rate for paid plans during synthetic bursts.
- Dashboards surface metrics with alerting for fallback_rate > 15% or enterprise_reserve_violation > 0.5%.
comments: 2026-02-26 - Maya Chen: Initial design sketched, shared with infra and runtime teams. Key asks: (a) runtime kernel must expose model-variant compatibility matrix, (b) quota buckets API needs slight addition to expose nominal_bucket sizes.

2026-03-02 - Lars Müller (review): Suggested replacing absolute quota thresholds with normalized percentage to avoid plan-size bias. Also recommended storing age as saturating 8-bit integer in allocator state to minimize memory overhead.

2026-03-05 - Ethan Rivera: Implemented POC scoring function in platform/allocator/service.go and added unit tests for age reset. PR #7682 created and linked in doc. Observability stubs wired to tracing.
2026-03-10 - Priya Nair (PM): Reviewed canary plan, approved 5% initial rollout in us-west. Requested that paid-tier degradations be logged as billable events for downstream billing reconciliation.

2026-03-12 - Security note from Noel Carter: No new secrets required; ensure logs that include tenant IDs are routed only to secure telemetry with PII filters. Marked security_review_required=false for now but flagged for infra audit during staging.

2026-03-14 - Ethan Rivera: Running integration sim against burst test vector set A (see allocator-sim/tests/burst-a.json). Early results: enterprise reserve holds, paid fallback rate ~9% on 5% canary. Pushing performance tuning for age multiplier to reduce oscillation.
